sources.findings: Seed may be started under cover or outdoors. Harden off transplants; keep multi-sown modules together. Sets are small bulbs with the pointed tip showing. Spring is the usual planting season; overwintering varieties are a separate option. Onion sets are spaced 10–15 cm apart.

Shallot sets multiply into clusters; a seed normally produces one bulb. Outdoor seedlings are thinned first to 5 cm, then 10 cm. Sets and module clumps need 15–20 cm. Spring is the default; suitable varieties allow autumn/winter planting on freely draining ground.

Producer confirms February–April seed sowing, with April direct sowing, 1.5 cm drills and 30 cm rows. Its 5 cm final spacing is cultivar-specific and closer than the RHS general 10 cm; retain packet-specific advice rather than use 5 cm as the universal mature spacing.
Producer corroborates the tips-showing set method and distinguishes single onion bulbs from shallot clusters. Its 10 cm onion and 15 cm shallot spacings lie within the RHS ranges.

Search result corroborates 1.5 cm onion seed depth. Proposal retains the current approximately 1.5 cm / 5/8 in pair; RHS onion depth is approximately 1.3 cm, while RHS shallot outdoor depth is 1.5 cm.

editorialDecisions: Separate seed-grown individual bulbs, intact module clumps and sets; retain full master notes.
Use general RHS spacing: single seed-grown shallots 10 cm; sets and clumps 15–20 cm. Kings Zebrune closer spacing is cultivar-specific.
Retain practical seed-depth pair 1.5 cm / 5/8 in.; distinguish it from tips-showing set depth.
Retain 30 cm / 12 in. bulb-crop rows and separate salad onion spacing.

Follow-up requested by John: replace Plant in spring with Plant in March–April. RHS calls the normal sets window early to mid-spring for both onions and shallots; March–April is the practical month interpretation, retaining separate overwintering notes.

artwork.brief: Transparent botanical watercolours: shallow covered seed; young seedlings; a soil cutaway with only the set tip above ground; one onion compared with a shallot cluster. No labels embedded in images.

approval: John approved the final changes on 1 October 2026: “That's good - I approve the changes.” This includes the separate seed/set routes, final illustrations and March–April set-planting caption in both A4 editions.
